AF.funFact: Afghanistan has changed its national flag several times since the 20th century, mostly using black, red and green.

AL.funFact: On Albania's flag, the red stands for bravery, strength, valour and bloodshed, while the black double-headed eagle is the traditional symbol of Albanians.

DZ.funFact: Algeria's flag, adopted on 3 July 1962, carries a red star and crescent, a symbol of Islam as the nation's prominent faith.

AO.funFact: Angola's flag was adopted on 11 November 1975, when the country became independent from Portugal.

AG.funFact: Antigua and Barbuda's flag was chosen in a competition with more than 600 local entries, won by artist and sculptor Sir Reginald Samuel.

AR.funFact: Argentina's sky-blue and white flag was created by Manuel Belgrano and first raised in Rosario on 27 February 1812.

AM.funFact: Armenia's flag was adopted on 24 August 1990, but it was first used during the First Republic of Armenia (1918–20).

AU.funFact: Australia's flag first flew as the Commonwealth blue ensign on 3 September 1901, chosen in a competition held after federation.

AT.funFact: Austria's red-white-red flag is one of the oldest national symbols still in use by a modern country, first recorded in 1230.

BE.funFact: Belgium's flag has the unusual proportions of 13:15, so unlike those of Switzerland and the Vatican City, it is not a perfect square.

BZ.funFact: Belize's flag was adopted on 21 September 1981, the day the country became independent.

BJ.funFact: Benin's flag was adopted in 1959 to replace the French Tricolour, and was the flag of the Republic of Dahomey until 1975.

BT.funFact: Bhutan's flag features the Druk, a dragon from Bhutanese mythology that alludes to the country's name in Dzongkha.

KW.funFact: Kuwait's is the only national flag featuring an acute trapezium.

LT.funFact: Lithuania's flag was adopted on 25 April 1918 during its first period of independence.

LU.funFact: Luxembourg's flag was first used between 1845 and 1848 but not officially adopted until 1993.

MG.funFact: Madagascar's flag was designed by Andrianome Ranaivosoa, an agent of the Malagasy National Geographic Institute.

MY.funFact: Malaysia's 14 stripes represent the equal status of the 13 member states and the federal territories, and the 14 points of the star represent their unity.

MM.funFact: Myanmar's current flag was adopted on 21 October 2010.

NL.funFact: The Dutch flag is the oldest tricolour flag in continuous use.

NZ.funFact: New Zealand's first internationally accepted national flag, the flag of the United Tribes, was adopted in 1834.

NI.funFact: Nicaragua's flag is one of the few that use purple, because of the rainbow in its coat of arms.

NE.funFact: Niger's flag has been in use since 1959, a year before the country's formal independence from French West Africa.

PS.funFact: Palestine's flag uses the pan-Arab colours, first combined in the current style during the 1916 Arab Revolt.

PA.funFact: Panama's Flag Day is celebrated on November 4, one day after the country's separation from Colombia.

PG.funFact: Papua New Guinea's flag shows the Southern Cross on one side and a silhouetted Raggiana bird-of-paradise on the other.

PY.funFact: Paraguay's is the only national flag in the world with a unique design on each side.

PE.funFact: Peru's Flag Day is celebrated on 7 June, the anniversary of the Battle of Arica.

PL.funFact: White and red were officially adopted as Poland's national colours in 1831.

PT.funFact: Portugal's flag was announced in 1910, following the revolution of 5 October 1910.

QA.funFact: Qatar's is the only national flag in the world with a width more than twice its height.

CG.funFact: The Republic of the Congo's flag was adopted in 1959 to replace the French Tricolour and was used until 1970.

RO.funFact: The colours of Romania's flag have been used on official insignia and symbols since the 14th century.

RU.funFact: Russia's white, blue and red design was first introduced by Tsar Peter the Great in 1693.

WS.funFact: Samoa's flag was designed with four stars in 1948, and the smaller fifth star was added in 1949.

SM.funFact: San Marino's coat of arms has a scroll bearing the word LIBERTAS, which means Freedom.
